letter: Thank you for the chance to look at 4800 126th Avenue North. This opinion of value rests on recent sales of comparable industrial buildings in the 33762 ZIP code.
Five comparable sales support a value range of $3.4 to $3.8 million for the 24,820-square-foot building. At the five-sale average of $145 per square foot, we value the property at about $3,600,000.

We built this from public records: the county appraiser, recorded sales, zoning, flood maps, and traffic counts. We have not seen leases, a rent roll, or the building's condition. Any of those could move the number, and we would like to see them.
I am glad to walk you through the comps and the math whenever it suits you.

paragraphs: Five comparable industrial sales in ZIP 33762 set the value. Average $145.55 per square foot, median $153.87.
The closest comp, 12625 40th Street N, is the same 1982 vintage and sold in April 2026 at $158 per square foot.
The building is owner-occupied with three business accounts on site, so rent and lease terms are the biggest unknown.
Zoning is M-1 Light Industrial. The site is in flood zone X, minimal hazard.

location.text: The site sits on the south side of 126th Avenue North at 47th Way North, just east of CR 611 (49th Street North). The surrounding blocks are light-industrial buildings of similar size.

cards.title: Zoning district
cards.text: Light Industrial. Pinellas Park administers zoning at this address, even though the mailing address reads Clearwater.

cards.title: Countywide plan category
cards.text: Employment, on the Forward Pinellas Countywide Plan Map. This is the tier above the zoning district, not a substitute for it.

cards.title: FEMA flood zone
cards.text: Area of minimal flood hazard. The preliminary map shows the same zone.

zoning.other: No historic district, overlay, or urban village applies, and the site is not in an opportunity zone.
zoning.confirm: We have not reviewed Pinellas Park's M-1 code. Permitted uses, outdoor storage, and any nonconforming status should be confirmed with the city before pricing a specific buyer's use.

market.headline: Pinellas County has a deep employment base, and this ZIP sits inside it.
market.callout: At the site. The building sits among similar light-industrial buildings, with direct access to CR 611.
market.sources: Sources: Census tract and ZIP data, county employment data (2026 Q1), 2025 traffic counts.

methodology.intro: We used the Sales Comparison Approach: what similar buildings recently sold for, per square foot, applied to this building.

steps.title: Screen
steps.text: Industrial buildings in ZIP 33762, 12,410 to 37,230 SF (about half to one and a half times the subject), sold since October 2024.

steps.title: Exclude
steps.text: We dropped 7 portfolio sales and 13 unqualified transfers. A 2005 sale of the subject itself is also left out.

steps.title: Compare
steps.text: Price per square foot of gross building area, so every sale is measured the same way.

steps.title: Reconcile
steps.text: The average and the median set the range. The five-sale average sets the single value.

methodology.note: We did not use the Income Approach. Public records carry no rents, leases, or operating expenses for this property.

comps.note: 12625 40th St N also sold in Oct 2024 for $3.0M ($104 per SF). It rose 52% in 18 months, so we treat it as the high-water mark, not the norm. 11286 47th St N #1 is a condo unit, a different product. The next page shows its effect on the average.

valuation.intro: Five comparable sales support a value range of $3.4 to $3.8 million. At the five-sale average of $145 per square foot, the property is valued at $3,600,000.

indications.label: Average without the condo unit (low end)

valuation.range_text: The average without the condo sets the low end and the five-sale median sets the high end, which gives $3.4 to $3.8 million. The five-sale average falls inside that range and is our single value. It is about $145 per square foot on the 24,820-square-foot gross building area.
could_move: Leases, tenants, and rent. We have not seen them.
The yard. At 32% coverage, the site carries more open land than most comps.

strategy.intro: The building is owner-occupied, so the right path depends on what you want to do with your own operation. Three options:

options.title: Sell and relocate
options.text: Market the building to owner-users and investors. Close, then move your operation on a timeline we set together.

options.title: Sell and lease back
options.text: Sell to an investor and stay as a tenant. This needs a lease, so rent and term become part of the price.

options.title: Hold and lease
options.text: Keep the building and lease some or all of it. We would need rent comps to set the asking rate.

strategy.note: Next steps: share current leases and the rent roll, if any. Tell us your timeline and whether you plan to stay in the building. We will add rent comps and a lease valuation to this opinion. Walk the building together to confirm condition.
